split: by person: even subject ids calibrate, odd subject ids are held out
scope: fingertip recordings, three-channel layout; one evaluation per record on the 1-9 s window
reference: ECG median-RR rate over the same window (>= 5 beats); ±5 bpm counts as correct

selection_rules.rule: Admitted-record precision >= 0.95 within ±5 bpm of the dataset's HR annotation, at least 30 admitted; then the most expert-good records admitted.
selection_rules.note: No grid point reached 0.95 on calibration (the best was 0.89). The dominant residual errors are half-rate readings where a motion or respiratory oscillation near 40-50 bpm outweighs a weak pulse. Revised once, before any held-out analysis.

selection_rules.rule: Admitted-record precision >= 0.90 within ±5 bpm of the ECG beat rate over the same window (records with >= 5 reference beats), at least 30 admitted; then the most expert-good records admitted; ties to the higher periodicity threshold, lower step threshold, higher rate floor, higher harmonic ratio.
selection_rules.note: The window-matched ECG reference replaces the whole-record annotation because it measures the same 8 seconds the algorithm sees.

interpretation: Precision is the share of admitted records whose rate is within ±5 bpm of the ECG; coverage is the share of expert-good records admitted; poor refusal is the share of expert-poor records refused. A camera pulse rate is not a medical measurement.
